scenario.title: Boundary Setting at a Community Event
scenario.context: A community BBQ event at a local park on a sunny Saturday afternoon. The event is bustling with people, children playing, BBQ grills sizzling, and a live band playing in the background.
scenario.description: Carla, a known community volunteer, is approached by John, the event coordinator, who wants her to take on another task. Carla is already busy with multiple responsibilities and needs to assertively communicate her boundaries.
scenario.speaker1_persona: Composed, reasonable and empathetic. She is someone who values her commitments and is aware of her limits.
scenario.speaker2_persona_1: High EQ - understanding, appreciative, and respectful of Carla's boundaries, not pushing her beyond her limits.
scenario.speaker2_persona_2: Low EQ - dismissive and impatient, trying to impose his needs without considering Carla's current workload.
scenario.speaker2_persona_3: Low EQ - manipulative and guilt-tripping, attempting to exploit Carla's dedication to the community to make her accept the additional task.
scenario.speaker2_persona_high: High EQ - understanding, appreciative, and respectful of Carla's boundaries, not pushing her beyond her limits.
scenario.speaker2_persona_low: Low EQ - dismissive and impatient, trying to impose his needs without considering Carla's current workload.

conversation.speaker: speaker1
conversation.text: John, I see you coming over here with that 'I need a favor' look.

conversation.speaker: speaker2
conversation.text: Carla, you know me too well! We could really use your help with coordinating the kids' games.

conversation.speaker: speaker1
conversation.text: I'd love to, John, but I'm already spread thin with the food and the decorations. I can't add another task to my plate.

conversation.speaker: speaker2
conversation.text: Well, I guess we'll have to find someone else then. You always make things look so effortless, Carla.

conversation.speaker: speaker1
conversation.text: Thank you, John. I think Sarah might be free, why don't you ask her?

conversation.speaker: speaker2
conversation.text: That's a great idea, Carla. I'll go find Sarah. Thanks for all that you're doing.
